source.quote: Arcam's own page for the ST25, read 2026-11-25. Bullet: « Supports up to 32 bit / 384 kHz Hires audio ». « Supported Bit depth: 16, 24, 32 »; « Supported sample rates (kHz): Up to 384 kHz »; « Supported media: ... DSD (up to 256) ... ». « Digital Audio Outputs 1x Coaxial (RCA), 1x Optical (Toslink) » - OUTPUTS, and the page lists no digital input at all. « USB Media (using USB-A mass storage input) », with no rate. Converter: « the latest Hyperstream iV DAC topology from ESS, in a balanced configuration ». No filter row.

facts.chip: « the latest Hyperstream iV DAC topology from ESS, in a balanced configuration ».

_une_page_de_conditions_qui_ne_dit_rien: arcam.co.uk HAS a terms page, linked as « Terms » in the footer, and its entire body is: « Contact us for details of our terms and conditions ». So the page exists, says nothing, and points to a contact form that was not used. There is no readable prohibition, and the footer carries « (c) 2026 Harman International Industries Ltd. » - the ordinary notice. Recorded in this shape because it is a third kind of answer, beside « no terms page » and « a terms page that forbids »: a terms page that defers.
_un_convertisseur_sans_la_moindre_entree: The page lists coaxial and optical as OUTPUTS and names no digital input. Music arrives over the network or from a USB stick. Fourth such device in the catalogue after LUMIN's X2, T3X and D3, and the same consequence: no inputs block, and the 384 kHz figure describes what the device will PLAY. A reader who takes « 1x Coaxial (RCA) » from the connections list and files it as an input would invent a socket that converts nothing.
